subject: Clarify: backup/log TTLs, prompt ephemerality, and DPA erasure SLAs
messages:
From: Ana Ruiz <dpo@medicohealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Data retention: backups, logs, prompts — DPA evidence request

Hi Olga,

The MedicoHealth privacy team is preparing our GDPR compliance sign-off for the upcoming integration and we need a concise set of statements + evidence about how Redwood handles customer data with respect to backups, logs, and prompt retention. Specifically: 

- Canonical retention windows: logs (access/ingest/audit), daily backups/snapshots, and any cold archival windows.
- How prompt text (API inputs) is persisted by default, and whether there's an option to set prompt ephemerality (and how that is implemented).
- The deletion/erase process when a DPA erasure request is received: expected timelines for live data, backups, and archived snapshots.
- Whether backups are immutable and if so how erasure obligations are handled (e.g., cryptographically making data inaccessible vs physical deletion).
- Evidence artifacts you can provide (policy excerpts, SOC 2 control IDs, sample audit log entries, or a certificate of erasure).

We aim to include this in our DPA amendment; can you provide the items above by close of business on Wed, Oct 7? If you'd prefer a short call, please propose 30 minutes.

Thanks,
Ana Ruiz
DPO, MedicoHealth

--
Note: please copy contracts/legal as appropriate (legal@medicohealth.com).

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Ana Ruiz <dpo@medicohealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 11:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Data retention: backups, logs, prompts — DPA evidence request

Ana — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Neha (legal) and Vivek (CS) so we can provide both the technical details and any contract language. High-level answers below; attaching a short policy summary and a draft erasure matrix for reference.

Summary (short):
- Logs: Hot/log-indexed retention is 90 days by default (live indexes for search/alerts). For customers that require longer audit windows we keep a cold log snapshot view for up to 13 months (search-disabled, access-control gated for forensics/audit).
- Backups & snapshots: Automated snapshot retention is 90 days for restore points in primary restore pools. Snapshots older than 90 days move to encrypted cold archive; archival TTL is 18 months by default.
- Prompt retention (API inputs): By default, hosted API request payloads (prompts) are retained for 30 days to support debugging, quality monitoring, and abuse detection. Customers may opt-in to extended retention or opt-out (ephemeral mode) at account level — in ephemeral mode prompts are never written to durable storage, only to memory and logs scrubbed.
- Deletion / erasure process:
  - Live stores: qualified erasure requests are reflected in primary stores within 24–72 hours (dependent on queued processing).
  - Snapshot purge: we run snapshot purge jobs weekly; once a snapshot is marked for deletion it's removed from index and scheduled for secure purge. Final material deletion for archived copies occurs within 30 days after the purge job (so total for archived snapshot removal can be up to ~60 days depending on when the purge job runs).
  - Immutable backups: where backups are write-once for legal/regulatory reasons, we make data cryptographically inaccessible (key revocation / shredding) immediately upon approved erasure request and record a verifiable event. Physical deletion follows normal retention lapse.
- Encryption & controls: All backups and archives are encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit. Access is role-gated and audited; SOC 2 control mapping is provided in the attached policy excerpt.

Attachments: backup_policy_summary.pdf (policy highlights) and dpa_erasure_matrix.xlsx (mapping of request type -> store -> expected action/timeline).

Next steps: happy to take a 30-min call; propose Tue Oct 6 10:00-10:30am ET or Wed Oct 7 09:00-09:30am ET. Also note: Neha will follow up on potential DPA amendment language for immutable backups.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Security & Privacy Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: backup_policy_summary.pdf (24kb stub), dpa_erasure_matrix.xlsx (12kb stub)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Ana Ruiz <dpo@medicohealth.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 09:20:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Data retention: backups, logs, prompts — DPA evidence request

Ana / Olga,

Thanks for the prompt reply and the attachments. A few clarifications we will include in the DPA amendment:

1) Prompt/payload handling: please confirm whether persisted prompts are stored with any direct customer identifiers (account ID, user ID) or whether we pseudonymize/hash identifiers before writing to durable stores. If identifiers are kept, we need to capture the exact fields in the DPA.

2) Erasure SLA expectations: for primary live data we accept the 24–72 hour window. For backups/snapshots we propose the following contractual language: Redwood will make data inaccessible within 30 days of a validated erasure request; where physical deletion is prevented by third-party immutable retention the provider will provide a signed attestation and render the data cryptographically inaccessible immediately. Please confirm you can commit to attestation artifacts and proof (audit log entries / job IDs).

3) Evidence artifacts: please include example SOC 2 control IDs that map to backups and key management (we will surface them to our audit team). Also provide a sample erasure certificate (redacted) that shows the event id, date, and scope.

If you can confirm the three points above and provide a redacted erasure certificate and SOC 2 control mapping, we can draft the DPA amendment and circulate to MedicoHealth legal. We'll plan to put the amendment into DocuSign for signatures once we have wording.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

On-call: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
